cli.verify: Killercoda-style tasks: goal → ordered steps (event steps must follow the previous event step; state steps are checked live) → complete
ux: check (and a Check button) · hint · solution · task · reset · clear · help
analytics: immersive_cli_cmd (verb + exit code only, never the raw command text)
immersive_cli_coach (action + level + step index only, never command text)
immersive_cli_review_card (sim + task + step index + why: solution | check-fail — never command text)
immersive_cli_voice (sim + kind: verb | command | none | error + ok — never the transcript)
cli.storage: localStorage il.immersiveCli.v1 (task completions + best command count, device only); CLI review cards in il.immersiveReview.v1 (device only)
cli.honesty: Simulated shell over the in-browser rules engine — real CLI syntax, computed output (kubectl/etcdctl/aws-shaped, not byte-identical). Not a real shell, container, cluster, AWS account or hosted lab fleet. Unmodelled commands say so instead of inventing output.

coach.benchmark: Killercoda Brain (2026): hint vs solution mode, hint offered after the 2nd failed verification, explains why a solution is not accepted
coach.ladder: check #1 on a step → diagnosis · check #2+ → diagnosis + tip (never the command) · solution → exact command
diagnosis: out of order (seen before the previous step verified)
right command family, wrong cluster state
coach.spatial: each step names authored glTF nodes (focus regex, unit-tested against the .glb); the player pulses them gold for ~9 s — also in WebXR; static stages list them
coach.voice: optional 'Lab Muse voice' toggle — browser speechSynthesis only (no cloud TTS, no key); hidden when unavailable
coach.honesty: Deterministic rules over the same in-browser sim state — not an LLM, not reading a real terminal, knows only what the drill models.

reviewCards.trigger: a free-play step where you typed `solution`, or failed `check` on it twice, becomes one spaced-repetition card (once per step per session)
reviewCards.store: the existing il.immersiveReview.v1 Leitner queue (key sim::cli:task:step); due CLI cards are served, never used as top-ups; domain mastery stays on predict checkpoints
reviewCards.review: /immersive/review/ re-mounts the drill's authored .glb with the simulated shell, replays the earlier steps from their own solutions, and grades the target step: verified without `solution` = recalled; `solution` / give-up = miss (box 0)
reviewCards.honesty: On-device Leitner scheduling — not FSRS, not a trained model, no server.

voice.api: Web Speech SpeechRecognition / webkitSpeechRecognition (feature-checked; the Speak button is hidden when unsupported)
voice.behaviour: lab verbs (check, hint, solution, task, reset, clear, help) run directly; spoken commands are normalised ("dash n" → -n, "dot" → ., snapped to this drill's vocabulary) into the input for you to check and press Enter — never auto-run
voice.honesty: Uses the browser's own speech recognition (some browsers send audio to their vendor's speech service). Interstitium receives no audio or transcript. Not an LLM.

cli.gatewayNote: Gateway API pack (2026-10-21) drives the gateway-api sim on the same authored ingress-gateway.glb. GatewayClass lab-gw (controllerName example.net/lab-gateway-controller) is a lab implementation computed by the rules engine — not Envoy Gateway, Istio, Cilium or NGINX Gateway Fabric, and not a live Gateway.
cli.nodeNote: Worker-node pack (2026-10-22) drives node-troubleshoot on the NEW authored node-troubleshoot.glb. systemd, journald, crictl, df and sed output is computed from sim state (shaped like the real tools, not byte-identical; journal lines are labelled representative). No VM, no real kubelet, no clock: durations such as node-monitor-grace-period and the 300s eviction toleration are explained, not simulated.
cli.serviceDnsNote: Service + DNS pack (2026-10-23) drives service-dns on the NEW authored service-dns.glb. Lookups go through the rules engine's resolv.conf model (search shop.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local, ndots:5) over four cluster records; nslookup / dig / CoreDNS log output is shaped like the real tools (labelled representative), not byte-identical. No live cluster, no real CoreDNS, no internet upstream, no clock: CrashLoopBackOff back-off and resolver timeouts are explained, not counted down. cli.cniNote: CNI pack (2026-10-27) drives cni-network on the authored cni-pod-network.glb (no new asset). Calico is the modelled CNI; calico.yaml and new-pool.yaml are trimmed lab stand-ins, and kubectl get/patch ippool stands in for calicoctl or the Calico API server (projectcalico.org/v3). The pool migration follows Calico's documented order (create the new pool, disable the old one, recreate pods). ping / curl / nslookup results are computed from the rules engine, shaped like busybox and curl output, not byte-identical. cli.meshNote: Service-mesh pack (2026-10-27) drives mesh-mtls on the authored service-mesh-sidecar.glb (no new asset). Istio semantics: STRICT resets plaintext clients, injection needs the namespace label and newly created pods, PERMISSIVE accepts both, istiod at zero leaves existing sidecars on their last config while the sidecar-injector webhook (failurePolicy Fail) blocks new pods. payments echoes headers like httpbin /headers, so X-Forwarded-Client-Cert shows an mTLS hop. istioctl output is computed and trimmed. Not CKA core; no live mesh, no real Envoy or istiod.
cli.cksNote: CKS pack (2026-10-29) drives cks-pod-security on the NEW authored cks-pod-security.glb. PodSecurity admission messages follow the built-in controller's format (violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest": …); /proc status, id, curl and the audit.k8s.io/v1 event are computed from sim state and labelled representative where shaped, not byte-identical. No live cluster, no real kubelet, kernel or seccomp, no clock: the static-pod restart after a manifest edit is explained, not waited for. cks_coverage.curriculum: cncf/curriculum CKS v1.34: Cluster Setup 15% · Cluster Hardening 15% · System Hardening 10% · Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities 20% · Supply Chain Security 20% · Monitoring, Logging and Runtime Security 20%

covered.Cluster Setup: NetworkPolicy default-deny / allow (cks-pod-security + netpol-isolation); CIS benchmark with kube-bench: kubelet anonymous auth, AlwaysAllow vs Webhook, read-only port, restart after a config edit, etcd data dir permissions, API server profiling (cks-cluster-hardening)
covered.Cluster Hardening: RBAC least privilege for ServiceAccounts (cks-pod-security + rbac-authz)
covered.System Hardening: seccomp RuntimeDefault vs Unconfined (cks-pod-security); AppArmor Localhost profiles: load with apparmor_parser, CreateContainerError when missing, deny-write (cks-runtime-security)
covered.Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities: Pod Security Standards / Admission (restricted); sandboxed container runtimes: RuntimeClass (handler, scheduling.nodeSelector, overhead.podFixed), the containerd handler, FailedCreatePodSandBox, a host-kernel bug under runc vs gVisor, uname -r / dmesg as evidence (cks-sandbox-runtime)
covered.Monitoring, Logging & Runtime Security: API server audit policy + log backend (cks-pod-security); Falco runtime detection, rule overrides, immutable containers (readOnlyRootFilesystem), audit vs runtime visibility (cks-runtime-security)
covered.Supply Chain Security: allowed registries (ValidatingAdmissionPolicy), Trivy scan gate + minimal base image, CycloneDX SBOM, cosign signing + admission signature verification, digest pinning (cks-supply-chain); static analysis of user workloads with kubesec and KubeLinter: score sums and exit codes, CI gates vs || true, ignore-check annotations, literal secrets vs secretKeyRef, runAsNonRoot over a root image (cks-static-analysis)

notCovered: keyless (Sigstore OIDC) signing; static analysis beyond the 8 modelled KubeLinter checks and the kubesec rules in this manifest (Dockerfile linting such as hadolint, Helm/Kustomize rendering, custom KubeLinter templates, kubesec as an admission webhook)

Kata Containers (a VM per pod) and gVisor beyond the modelled behaviour (platform choice ptrace/KVM, syscall compatibility gaps, performance cost, runsc flags); RuntimeClass on managed clouds (GKE Sandbox)
Falco rule authoring beyond one lab rule, Falcosidekick / alert routing, Tetragon / Tracee
kube-bench checks beyond the five modelled (file ownership/permissions of manifests and PKI, controller-manager and scheduler flags, kubelet TLS / rotation)
cks_coverage.muskVerdict: Closer/NO until live UE host + hosted fleet exist

contexts.default: on (?contexts=0 for a paper without contexts)
contexts.mechanism: own PRNG stream per seed (salt 'kube'): each scene on the paper is one cluster with a seeded context name, plus one decoy context no task uses; the first task starts on the decoy and every later task starts where the previous one left the shell; the task, name and fault draws are unchanged
contexts.results: per task: switched before the first kubectl command or not, and how many kubectl commands hit another context; summary line in [data-il-ts-contexts]; attempts store wrongContext
contexts.honesty: The other contexts are empty stand-in clusters, not modelled clusters. Switching is not a scored checkpoint: as on the exam, forgetting it means the work lands elsewhere. The scene dim is a study cue the real exam does not give. Context names are authored, not the exam's.

faults.host_token: node01 (re-drawn per seed: compute-03 | wk-east-2 | k8s-w7)
faults.mechanism: per (seed, incident) PRNG stream ('#fault') picks one authored fault; each fault is its own CLI task (setup, steps, ticket) on the same authored scene; the v1.0.0 task draw and the v1.1.0 name draw are unchanged; variants off (?variants=0) gives the canonical fault
faults.honesty: 7 hand-authored faults over the 3 kube-bench incidents, not procedurally generated faults; the other 21 incidents vary names over one staged fault. node01 is the same simulated rules engine (no VM, no real ssh).

variants.default: on (lobby checkbox data-il-ts-variants, or ?variants=0 for a drill-replay paper)
variants.fixed_tasks_note: fixed names on the canonical fault only; since v1.2.0 (2026-11-11) these three draw a fault variant (see cks_paper.faults) and the node01 host name instead
variants.mechanism: per (seed, task) PRNG picks one replacement per canonical token; a whole-word canonical<->variant swap (an involution) is applied to the typed line before the rules engine and to every printed line after it; pools are unit-tested never to occur in the CLI packs or sims
variants.honesty: Surface variants (names, port, registry, image tags) over the same staged faults, not new fault logic. CIS ids, kubelet ports and system paths stay real; authored 3D node names and review cards stay canonical.

cks_paper.grading: ILTroubleshootExam.gradeIncident / stage (same partial-credit rules: 1 per verified checkpoint, hint = 0.5, solution off)
cks_paper.sources: all 21 tasks of the six CKS CLI packs + rbac-authz least-privilege / revoke + netpol-isolation lock-api; since 2026-11-11 the 4 multi-node CIS tasks serve as fault variants of the 3 kube-bench incidents
cks_paper.draw: domains heaviest first (ties shuffled per seed), one task per domain per round, then shuffled: 6 tasks cover all six domains, 3 tasks cover the three 20% domains
cks_paper.score: blueprint-weighted % (CNCF CKS weights 15/15/10/20/20/20) renormalised over the domains the paper tested; unweighted mean shown alongside; untested domains listed, never counted as passed
cks_paper.weakest: domain with the most points at stake = weight x (1 - score); links to the drill of the lowest-scoring task in it
cks_paper.remediation: first missed/hinted checkpoint per task -> CLI review card (src 'cks-paper'); /immersive/review/ CKS queue (review v1.4.0 queue({track:'CKS'}))
cks_paper.honesty: Simulated shell over the in-browser rules engine. Not a live cluster, not killer.sh, not the CNCF CKS; Falco, AppArmor, kube-bench, kubesec, KubeLinter, Trivy, cosign and gVisor are rules-engine stand-ins.
